vignettes.body:
Alice Chan, CFA is a senior partner at a large investment bank which has adopted the CFA Institute Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct. Alex Berg is her supervisor.
Chan has been working with an internal data science team to develop a machine learning model to improve the bank's forecast of IPO prices. Chan needs to provide a formal recommendation of the model. In its last meeting with Chan, the data science team advised that adding several new variables to the model resulted in a statistically significant increase in forecast accuracy. However, Chan was not clear on how the new variables would improve the accuracy and considers whether to complete the following steps to finalize her recommendation:
Step 1: Review the technical aspects and programming of the model;
Step 2: Review the model factors and parameters to better understand its assumptions and limitations.
Chan receives a call from a client requesting a report on the telecommunications industry. Chan knows that she will not complete a full report because she plans to leave the bank to start her own private equity firm. Chan recalls another partner published a telecommunications industry report last month. However, that partner left the bank shortly after publication and is not available for any follow-up questions. Chan advises the client of the partner's report and forwards it, without changes, to the client.
Chan provides her resignation to Berg, effective in 10 business days. Chan expects to remain at the bank during the notice period to transition her client portfolios and to ensure that she leaves the bank on good terms. However, after reviewing the bank's standard policy for an employee's departure, Chan realizes that she must notify her clients and provide an alternative contact person. Accordingly, on the same day that she submits her resignation notice, Chan contacts all of her clients, informing them of her planned departure and providing Berg's contact information. If clients ask about her departure, Chan informs them she is starting her own firm. Immediately after contacting her clients, Chan updates her social media profile, which includes personal and professional contacts and information on the product offerings of her new firm.
Several weeks later, at her new firm, Chan receives an email from a client who is upset about finding significant errors in a research report provided by one of Chan's new employees. The client mentions the errors to Chan and suggests that Chan did not sufficiently review the report before publication. Chan is surprised by these errors because she has established a compliance process to validate all research reports and findings. Specifically, Chan validated the referenced sources and believed the analysis to be sound when the employee sent the report. Chan calls the employee into her office to review the client's concern. The employee acknowledges the errors, one of which included entering a stock price increase, rather than a stock price decrease, in the model used. Chan updates the client and commits to reviewing the firm's compliance process.

questions.q: With regard to the machine learning model, to be in compliance with the Standards, Chan must complete:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because Step 1, to review the technical aspects and programming of the model, is beyond the requirements of the Standard. Members and candidates are not required to become experts in the technical aspect of the models.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Chan is not required to complete Step 1 to be in compliance with the Standards. Members and candidates are not required to become experts in every technical aspect of the models. Only Step 2 is required to be compliant with the Standards.

questions.q: Did Chan violate the Standards by sending the previously prepared telecommunications industry report to the client?
options: Yes, because the author of the report no longer works at the bank
Yes, because she knowingly provided work completed by another analyst
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because research and models developed while employed by a firm are the property of the firm. The firm retains the right to continue using the work completed after a member or candidate has left the organization.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Chan advises the client of the pre-existing report and shares the report without making any changes or any representations that Chan completed the work herself.

questions.q: With regard to informing her clients of her planned departure and updating her social media profile, did Chan violate the Standards?
options: Yes, because of the timing of her updating her social media accounts
Yes, because of the timing of when she informed clients that she was starting her own firm
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because publicly updating her social media to include references to the new firm and product offering would be detrimental and potentially cause harm to her current employer and is a violation of the Standards. 
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Chan followed her employer's policies and procedures by notifying clients immediately, so there was no violation. Once notice is provided to the employer of the intent to resign, the member or candidate must follow the employer's policies and procedures related to notifying clients of his or her planned departure.

questions.q: With regard to the error in the research report, did Chan violate the Standards?
options: Yes, because she failed to detect the error
Yes, because she failed to have an adequate system for supervision
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the data entry error (a stock price increase, rather than a decrease) was missed by both the analyst and Chan but that does not constitute a violation of the Standards.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Chan had an established compliance program in place prior to the occurrence of the violation. The Standard requires that members and candidates with supervisory responsibility make reasonable efforts to prevent and detect violations by ensuring the establishment of effective compliance systems. Chan had established a compliance procedure and processes at her firm and validated the report before publication.

vignettes.body:
Emily Silva is an equity analyst working at a US-based investment consulting firm. She values the equity of four publicly traded firms, Firm A, Firm B, Firm C, and Firm D.
Silva examines whether the equity of Firm A, a manufacturing company, is mispriced. She gathers the information (in $ millions) in Exhibit 1 based on the most recent year in order to calculate Firm A's FCFF. Firm A's tax rate is 30%.
Exhibit 1
EBITDA | 200
Depreciation expense | 20
Interest expense | 30
Net borrowing | 44
Investment in fixed capital | 27
Investment in working capital | 15
Silva then estimates the intrinsic value of Firm A's equity based on a declining growth two-stage model. The market value of Firm A's debt is $450 million. Firm A's cost of equity is 12%, and its WACC is 10%. Exhibit 2 shows Silva's projections of Firm A's FCFF (in $ millions) for the next three years. Silva assumes that FCFF will grow at a constant annual rate of 3% after Year 3.
Exhibit 2
#  | Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3
Projected FCFF | 160 | 180 | 190
Next, Silva evaluates Firm B for a corporate client interested in acquiring a controlling position in the firm. The client expects the acquisition to result in significant operating synergies. Firm B has a positive FCFE, most of which is paid out in dividends. Silva expects Firm B to continue to have an unstable capital structure because its use of debt changes from year to year. Silva identifies the most appropriate valuation approach for Firm B.
Another client asks Silva to evaluate a pairs trade that involves two publicly traded firms, Firm C and Firm D. Both firms operate in the copper mining industry. They are both profitable and close competitors. In addition to owning copper reserves, both firms manufacture electrical wires. The electrical wire segment comprises approximately one-third of each firm's revenues. For the pairs trade, Silva wants to evaluate which firm to buy and which firm to sell using an appropriate valuation approach.

questions.q: Firm A's FCFF (in $ millions) for the most recent year is:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because it ignores the tax rate for depreciation expense:
FCFF = $200(1 – 30%) + $20 – $27 – $15 = $140 + $20 – $27 – $15 = $118
The correct formula that calculates FCFF using EBIT is:
FCFF = EBIT(1 – Tax rate) + Dep – FCInv – WCInv
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because it represents the FCFE and uses all of the information provided in the exhibit.
FCFE = FCFF – Int (1 – Tax rate) + Net borrowing
FCFE = EBITDA(1 – Tax rate) + Dep(Tax rate) – FCInv – WCInv – Int (1 – Tax rate) + Net borrowing
where:
Int: Interest expense
Net borrowing: Net new borrowing
FCFE = $200(1 – 30%) + $20(30%) – $27 – $15 – $30(1– 30%) + $44
= $140 + $6 – $27 – $15 – $21 + $44 = $127

questions.q: The intrinsic value of Firm A's equity (in $ millions), as estimated by Silva, should be closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because this answer uses the cost of equity as the discount rate (instead of WACC). Below are the resulting incorrect figures obtained for the intermediate steps:
 	Year 1	Year 2	Year 3
Projected FCFF ($ millions)	$160	$180	$190
PV at 12% ($ millions)	$142.86	$143.49	$135.24
TV3 = $195.7 / (12% – 3%) = $2,174.44 million
Present value of TV3 = $2,174.44 / (1.12)3 = $1,547.73
The total present value of future FCFF (Intrinsic value of the firm) = $142.86 + $143.49 + $135.24 + $1,547.73 = $1,969.32
Intrinsic value of equity = $1,969.32 – $450 = $1,519.32
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because this answer ignores the subtraction of debt in Step 2. This figure represents the estimated intrinsic value of the firm (i.e., the present value of future FCFFs of $2,537.43).

questions.q: Which of the following is the most appropriate valuation approach for Firm B?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because of two reasons. First, DDM uses required return on equity as the discount rate, which is more sensitive to changes in financial leverage than the WACC. Second, the client is interested in a controlling position, which gives them the ability to change the use of free cash flows. For example, future dividends might be projected to decrease if the client intends to use the firm's free cash flow to serve the debt. In such a scenario, the use of DDM will seriously understate the value of the firm's equity and therefore be inappropriate.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the capital structure is unstable. FCFE uses required return on equity as the discount rate, which is more sensitive to changes in financial leverage than the WACC, making the use of FCFE inappropriate.
C. Correct.

questions.q: Which of the following valuation approaches is the most appropriate for Silva to use when evaluating the pairs trade involving Firm C and Firm D?
options: An asset-based valuation adjusted for conglomerate discount
A price-to-EBITDA-based comparables valuation adjusted for lack of marketability discount
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because of two reasons. First, both firms generate significant revenue from industrial electrical wiring sales and an asset-based approach is less suitable to value this segment. Second, conglomerate discount applies for companies that operate unrelated segments. Conglomerate discount refers to the concept that the market applies a discount to the stock of a company operating in multiple and unrelated businesses compared to the stock of companies with narrower focuses.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because lack of marketability discount does not apply to either firm as they are both publicly traded.

vignettes.body:
Antoinette Barilla is a credit advisor reviewing a client's corporate bond portfolio.
The portfolio holds an A-rated bond issued by Better Corp. The bond has a YTM of 3.0% and a credit spread of 110 bps. Barilla calculates the expected 1-year total return for the bond using the 1-year credit rating migration information in Exhibit 1.
Exhibit 1
# Credit Rating Migration | Transition Probability | Expected Price Change
From A to A | 90% | 0.0%
From A to BBB | 9% | –2.0%
From A to BB | 1% | –3.0%
Barilla considers adding another bond to the client's portfolio. She evaluates the credit term structure for Grocery, Inc. Grocery is offering a new bond issue to refinance short-term debt with longer-maturity debt. Barilla notes that the new issue has a tighter bid–offer spread and a higher credit rating than Grocery's previously issued bonds. Barilla expects the credit spread curve for Grocery bonds to steepen after the new issue.
Barilla recommends the client enter into a bond–CDS basis trade on a corporate bond issued by Animal Supplies Company. The bond currently yields 5.0%. A comparable-maturity CDS contract has a credit spread of 290 bps. Barilla notes that the client can borrow at the 1.2% market reference rate. She calculates the profit of the basis trade if convergence were to occur between the bond and the CDS contract.
Finally, Barilla reviews a combined position where the client owns $1 million of Bond D issued by Material Corporation, along with $1 million of CDS protection on Material where Bond D is the reference obligation. Material has issued three bonds, Bonds C, D, and E, that rank equally with respect to the priority of claims. Barilla estimates that, in the event of a default, Bond C would trade at 20% of par, Bond D at 30% of par, and Bond E at 40% of par. If a default occurs, the client will cash settle the CDS.

questions.q: Based on the credit rating migration information, the expected 1-year total return for the Better Corp. bond is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the change in value is subtracted from the credit spread.
(0.90 × 0.0%) + (0.09 × –2.0%) + (0.01 × –3.0%) = –0.21%
1.10%-0.21% = 0.89%≈ 0.9%
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because, in addition to subtracting the change in value, the credit spread is subtracted from the YTM.
(0.90 × 0.0%) + (0.09 × –2.0%) + (0.01 × –3.0%) = –0.21%
3.00% – 0.21% - 1.10% = 1.69% ≈ 1.7% 
C. Correct.

questions.q: Barilla's expectation regarding the credit spread curve for Grocery, Inc. is best supported by the new bond issue's:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because Barilla notes that the new issue will have a higher credit rating than previously issued bonds and she expects the Grocery, Inc. credit spread curve to steepen after the new issue. The credit term structure for the most highly rated securities tends to be either flat or slightly upward sloping.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Barilla notes that the new issue has a tighter bid–offer spread and she expects the Grocery, Inc. credit spread curve to steepen after the new issue. The steepening effect may be partially offset by a tighter bid–offer spread for longer credit maturities.

questions.q: If convergence were to occur, the basis trade on Animal Supplies would capture a profit closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the CDS credit spread (not the MRR) is subtracted from the bond yield.
5.0% – 2.9% = 2.1%
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the MRR is subtracted from the CDS credit spread (instead of from the bond yield):
2.9% – 1.2% = 1.7%
Then this result is subtracted from the bond yield:
5.0% – 1.7% = 3.3%

questions.q: If Material Corporation defaults, the total proceeds from the client's Bond D and CDS position would be closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the CDS payoff should be based on the lowest recovery rate, not the highest.
This response is based on an understanding that cash settlement is different than physical settlement, but it incorrectly calculates the proceeds based on the highest recovery rate. The highest CDS recovery rate is based on Bond E at 40% of par.
CDS: (1 – 40%) × $1 million = $600,000 
Bond: 30% × $1 million = $300,000
Total proceeds: $600,000 + $300,000 = $0.9 million
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the CDS payoff should be based on the lowest recovery rate.
This response incorrectly calculates the proceeds from physical settlement by using the recovery rate of Bond D. The CDS physical settlement recovery rate based on Bond D is 30% of par.
CDS: (1 – 30%) × $1 million = $700,000 
Bond: 30% × $1 million = $300,000
Total proceeds: $700,000 + $300,000 = $1.0 million
C. Correct.

vignettes.body:
Andrea Castillo is an investment consultant specializing in alternative investments. One of her clients is the Busilak family office. The Busilak family office considers allocating a portion of its portfolio to hedge funds. Castillo identifies three hedge funds as potential investments for Busilak, Fund X, Fund Y, and Fund Z.
Castillo assesses the performance of each fund under a crisis scenario where the stock market index falls and stock market volatility rises. Castillo estimates a conditional factor risk model using monthly returns for the past 10 years. Exhibit 1 provides the factor beta estimates of the model. All coefficient estimates are statistically significant.
Exhibit 1
#  | Fund X | Fund Y | Fund Z
Normal Times Exposures |  |  | 
Intercept | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00
Equity risk factor (EQU) | –0.19 | 0.43 | –0.03
Volatility risk factor (VOL) | 0.09 | 0.16 | 0.01
Crisis Times Exposures (Incremental) |  |  | 
DEQU | 0.09 | 0.16 | –0.02
DVOL | 0.27 | –0.18 | 0.03
DEQU is the product of the equity risk factor, EQU, and a dummy variable that equals 1 during crisis periods and 0 otherwise. DVOL is the product of the volatility risk factor, VOL, and the same dummy variable.
The family office decides to add hedge funds to the current portfolio to form a new portfolio. The family office's objective is to choose a new portfolio based on maximized risk-adjusted return with risk measured by downside deviation. Exhibit 2 provides the risk and return characteristics of three simulated combined portfolios, with each holding a 20% hedge fund allocation.
Exhibit 2
# Portfolio | Standard Deviation | Sharpe Ratio | Sortino Ratio
Current portfolio + Fund X | 7.50% | 0.32 | 0.48
Current portfolio + Fund Y | 8.80% | 0.43 | 0.70
Current portfolio + Fund Z | 7.62% | 0.45 | 0.68
Another client of Castillo is Pearl University, whose endowment is currently invested in stocks and bonds. Pearl plans to gain long exposure to energy commodities and considers investing in futures contracts.
Castillo analyzes a recent trade that involved a long position in crude oil futures. The fully collateralized position was held for six months and realized a price return of 6% and a roll return of 4%. The risk-free rate is 2% per year. Castillo computes the 6-month total return for this position.
Castillo suggests that, instead of futures, Pearl could also use a total return swap based on any of the following broad-based major commodity indexes: the Rogers International Commodity Index (RICI), the Bloomberg Commodity Index (BCOM), or the S&P GSCI. Castillo determines the most appropriate reference index for the swap if the objective is to maximize exposure to energy commodities.

questions.q: Which fund should be expected to perform best under the crisis scenario?
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because, when equity prices fall and volatility rises, the fund that would perform best is the one with the smallest equity risk factor beta and the largest volatility risk factor beta.
During crisis periods, Fund Y has historically had the largest equity risk factor beta (0.59) and the smallest volatility risk factor beta (–0.02). Fund Y is expected to perform worst.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because, when equity prices fall and volatility rises, the fund that would perform best is the one with the smallest equity risk factor beta and the largest volatility risk factor beta.
During crisis periods, Fund X is expected to perform better than Fund Z. Fund X has historically had a larger negative equity risk factor beta than Fund Z (–0.10 versus –0.05) and a larger positive volatility risk factor beta (0.36 versus 0.04).

questions.q: Which of the following funds should the family office add to the current portfolio to meet its objective?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the addition of Fund X to the current portfolio results in the lowest (not highest) Sortino ratio. The Sharpe ratio measures risk-adjusted performance, where risk is defined as standard deviation, so it penalizes both upside and downside variability. The Sortino ratio measures risk-adjusted performance, where risk is defined as downside deviation, so it penalizes only downside variability below a minimum target return.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the addition of Fund Z to the current portfolio does not result in the highest Sortino ratio. Instead, it results in the highest Sharpe ratio. The Sharpe ratio measures risk-adjusted performance, where risk is defined as standard deviation, so it penalizes both upside and downside variability. The Sortino ratio measures risk-adjusted performance, where risk is defined as downside deviation, so it penalizes only downside variability below a minimum target return.

questions.q: The 6-month total return for the crude oil futures position is:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the collateral return is omitted from the calculation.
Price return = 6%
Roll return = 4%
Total return (incorrect) = 6% + 4% = 10%
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the given collateral return, which is annualized, is not converted to a 6-month return.
Price return = 6%
Roll return = 4%
Collateral return (incorrect) = 2%
Total return (incorrect) = 6% + 4% + 2% = 12%

questions.q: The most appropriate reference index for Pearl’s swap is the:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because Pearl aims to maximize exposure to energy commodities, so the most appropriate index to use as a basis for the commodity swap is the one which has the highest sector weight on energy.  
The RICI uses a fixed-weighting scheme to allocate exposure among 38 different commodities. RICI uses the fixed weight weighting method.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because Pearl aims to maximize exposure to energy commodities, so the most appropriate index to use as a basis for the commodity swap is the one which has the highest sector weight on energy.
BCOM's rules of index construction also place caps on the size of the sectors (33% maximum) and floors on individual commodities (2% minimum). These differences mean that very different index composition and weights can occur. For example, the energy sector currently dominates the S&P GSCI (as high as 80% weight), whereas the BCOM’s exposure is much lower (approximately 30%).
C. Correct.

vignettes.body:
Eto Partners is a multinational investment firm managing portfolios for institutions and high-net-worth individuals. Eto has adopted the Standards as part of its ethics and compliance policy. The firm's policy requires employees obtain pre-approval of personal trades in all securities held in Eto portfolios.
Annika Lyden manages Eto's Epic equity fund which focuses on the health care and life sciences sectors. Stefan Meier, an analyst that reports to Lyden, reviews Proctivi, a small-cap firm developing an experimental arthritis treatment. Proctivi is not currently held in any Eto portfolios. Meier believes the company has strong growth potential and recommends its purchase. After discussing the recommendation, Lyden and Meier conclude it is too risky for the Epic fund but will revisit the recommendation in 12 months. After the discussion, Lyden decides to purchase 5,000 shares of Proctivi for her personal account.
Eto's research department releases an updated economic forecast which projects a significant increase in market volatility over the next 12 months. One of Lyden's high-net-worth clients reviews the forecast and expresses concern about the corresponding impact on his portfolio. Lyden suggests the client use a structured product developed by Eto which has a return tied to changes in market volatility. Lyden provides the client with a report describing the basic characteristics and inputs of the product, how it is constructed, and the amount of leverage in the structure. She does not include specific details about the model used to develop the product or details of how inputs were determined. The report only provides the expected performance under an increase in market volatility because that is the client's primary concern.
Lyden asks Meier to participate in a presentation to a class of finance students at a nearby university. None of the students are clients of Eto. Meier shares his long-term forecast and Eto's investment recommendation for Balmtrex with the students. Balmtrex is a small-cap firm that has developed a successful cancer treatment. He states his belief that Balmtrex has substantial upside potential and that it is suitable for all investors with a long-term investment horizon. He tells the students, "This is an awesome investment for people like yourselves." He does not discuss related risks.
Lyden is considering adding to the Epic fund's investment in InG Pharma. During a lunch meeting, a well-respected biotech industry analyst tells Lyden that InG Pharma has a promising anti-viral drug in a late-stage drug trial. He believes the drug will come to market in the next 24 months and will significantly increase the company's revenue. Following the conversation, Lyden purchases an additional 50,000 shares of InG for the Epic fund. Lyden shares the analyst's information with a colleague who manages another fund for Eto.

questions.q: Does Lyden's purchase of Proctivi for her personal account violate the Standards?
options: Yes, she should have obtained pre-approval for the purchase
Yes, she should follow Epic's investment methodology and not purchase Proctivi
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because she doesn't need to obtain preapproval. She is only required to get preapproval for securities held in Eto portfolios. Proctivi is not held in any of the firm's portfolios so pre-approval is not required.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Epic's investment methodology does not apply to Lyden's personal trading activities. She is free to purchase investments that are unsuitable for Epic.

questions.q: Does Lyden violate the Standards in providing the structured product report to her client?
options: Yes, because her report didn't provide specific details about the model or the inputs
Yes, because she should disclose expected performance for both an increase and a decrease in market volatility
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because members and candidates must adequately disclose the general market-related risks and the risks associated with the use of complex financial instruments that are deemed significant. In addition, the member or candidate who prepares the report must include those elements that are important to the analysis and conclusions of the report so that the reader can follow and challenge the report’s reasoning. Lyden's report only discusses performance with an increase in market volatility, not a decrease in market volatility.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the member or candidate who prepares the report must include those elements that are important to the analysis and conclusions of the report so that the reader can follow and challenge the report’s reasoning. A report writer who has done adequate investigation may emphasize certain areas, touch briefly on others, and omit certain aspects deemed unimportant. Lyden included the basic characteristics of the product but doesn't include specific details about the model and the inputs. The specifics of a complex model do not need to be shared.
C. Correct.

questions.q: Does Meier violate the Standards with his recommendation of Balmtrex to the finance students?
options: Yes, because he did not discuss the risks of investing in Balmtrex
Yes, because he did not consider the suitability of the investment for the students
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because Standard III(C) requires that members and candidates who are in an investment advisory relationship with clients consider carefully the needs, circumstances, and objectives of the clients when determining the appropriateness and suitability of a given investment or course of investment action. The students are not clients receiving investment advice so there is no investment advisory relationship so there is no requirement to discuss the risk around the investment.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Standard III(C) requires that members and candidates who are in an investment advisory relationship with clients consider carefully the needs, circumstances, and objectives of the clients when determining the appropriateness and suitability of a given investment or course of investment action. The students are not clients receiving investment advice so there is no investment advisory relationship and therefore no need to consider the suitability for them.

questions.q: With regard to InG Pharma, does Lyden violate the Standards regarding material nonpublic information?
options: Yes, because she purchased additional shares for the fund
Yes, because she shared the analyst's information with a colleague
questions.why:
A. Correct. Correct because, according to Standard II(A) regarding material nonpublic information, the information about the drug trial is not material nonpublic information. Lyden is allowed to share the information with a colleague and trade on the information.
In addition to the substance and specificity of the information, the source or relative reliability of the information also determines materiality. The less reliable a source, the less likely the information provided would be considered material. Additionally, information about trials of a new drug, product, or service under development from qualified personnel involved in the trials is likely to be material, whereas educated conjecture by subject experts not connected to the trials is unlikely to be material.
The source of the information is a well-respected industry analyst expressing his opinion on the prospects of the new drug driving InG Pharma's future sales. It is unlikely that his opinion would be considered material.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the information is not material non-public information so she is allowed to purchase shares using this information as an input into her valuation model. 
In addition to the substance and specificity of the information, the source or relative reliability of the information also determines materiality. The less reliable a source, the less likely the information provided would be considered material. Additionally, information about trials of a new drug, product, or service under development from qualified personnel involved in the trials is likely to be material, whereas educated conjecture by subject experts not connected to the trials is unlikely to be material.
The source of the information is a well-respected industry analyst expressing his opinion on the prospects of the new drug driving InG Pharma's future sales. It is unlikely that his opinion would be considered material.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the information is not material non-public information so she is allowed to share it with her research analyst. 
In addition to the substance and specificity of the information, the source or relative reliability of the information also determines materiality. The less reliable a source, the less likely the information provided would be considered material. Additionally, information about trials of a new drug, product, or service under development from qualified personnel involved in the trials is likely to be material, whereas educated conjecture by subject experts not connected to the trials is unlikely to be material.

vignettes.body:
Jennifer Lee is analyzing the performance of Belle, a global consumer products company. Belle is located in the eurozone and uses the EUR as its functional and presentation currency. Belle reports under IFRS and has a 31 December year end.
Belle operates predominantly in the UK. Lee gathers the information about EUR/GBP exchange rates (amount of EUR per 1 GBP) in Exhibit 1.
Exhibit 1
#  | EUR/GBP Exchange Rate
16 November, most recent year | 1.186
31 December, most recent year | 1.176
18 January, current year | 1.193
Lee notes that Belle purchased inventory for GBP 500,000 from an unaffiliated UK company on 16 November of the most recent year. The transaction was settled on 18 January of the current year.
A UK-based subsidiary of Belle uses the GBP as its functional currency. Lee gathers the information about the subsidiary's net sales growth in Exhibit 2.
Exhibit 2
#  | Most Recent Year | Two Years Ago
Volume growth | 5% | 3%
Price growth | 2% | 1%
Foreign currency effect | 3% | –1%
Net sales growth | 10% | 3%
Belle uses the current rate method to translate its subsidiaries' financial statements. In contrast, Belle's primary competitor uses the temporal method to translate its subsidiaries' financial statements. Lee considers how each company should report its cumulative translation adjustment under the method used.
Lindo is Belle's wholly owned subsidiary in Country F, a hyperinflationary economy that uses the currency FCX. Lindo purchased land for FCX 61,390,000 on 1 January two years ago. The EUR/FCX exchange rates (amount of EUR per 1 FCX) and Country F's inflation rates are shown in Exhibit 3.
Exhibit 3
Exchange rate on 1 January two years ago | 0.0149 EUR/FCX
Exchange rate on 31 December of the most recent year | 0.0086 EUR/FCX
Inflation rate for two years ago | 38%
Inflation rate for the most recent year | 51%

questions.q: As a result of the inventory purchase, Belle should recognize a foreign currency transaction loss of:
options: EUR 5,000 in the most recent year.
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because Belle would recognize an unrealized foreign currency gain, not loss, of EUR 593,000 – EUR 588,000 = EUR 5,000 at the end of the most recent year.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because this represents the net foreign currency loss from transaction date to settlement date. Belle owed GBP 500,000, which would cost EUR 593,000 (GBP 500,000 × EUR/GBP 1.186). At the settlement date, Belle would pay EUR 596,500 (GBP 500,000 × EUR/GBP 1.193). The total foreign currency loss in the current year is EUR 3,500 (EUR 596,500 – EUR 593,000).

questions.q: From two years ago to the most recent year, the increase in the UK-based subsidiary's sustainable sales growth rate was:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because this represents the change in the growth of volume (5% – 3%) and does not consider the effect of the change in the growth of price (2% – 1% = 1%).
For a multinational company, sales growth is driven not only by changes in volume and price but also by changes in the exchange rates between the reporting currency and the currency in which sales are made. Arguably, growth in sales that comes from changes in volume or price is more sustainable than growth in sales that comes from changes in exchange rates. Further, management arguably has greater control over growth in sales resulting from greater volume or higher price than from changes in exchange rates.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because this represents the change in the growth of net sales (10% – 3%), which includes the effect of foreign currency changes (3% – (–1%) = 4%). 
For a multinational company, sales growth is driven not only by changes in volume and price but also by changes in the exchange rates between the reporting currency and the currency in which sales are made. Arguably, growth in sales that comes from changes in volume or price is more sustainable than growth in sales that comes from changes in exchange rates.

questions.q: Belle should report its cumulative translation adjustment as:
options: a component of other operating income.
a separate component of stockholders' equity.
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because this represents a potential treatment of a foreign currency transaction and not a translation adjustment. The two most common treatments (of foreign currency transaction gains and losses, not translation adjustments) are either (1) as a component of other operating income/expense or (2) as a component of non-operating income. Belle uses the current rate method, and when the current rate method is used, the cumulative translation adjustment needed to keep the translated balance sheet in balance is reported as a separate component of stockholders’ equity.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because Belle uses the current rate method and this represents treatment under the temporal method. Under both international and US accounting standards, when the temporal method is used, the translation adjustment needed to keep the translated balance sheet in balance is reported as a gain or loss in net income.
It also represents a potential treatment of a foreign currency transaction, not a translation adjustment. The two most common treatments (of foreign currency transaction gains and losses, not translation adjustments) are either (1) as a component of other operating income/expense or (2) as a component of non-operating income.
C. Correct.

questions.q: At the end of the most recent year, the value of Lindo's land (in EUR thousands) on its consolidated balance sheet should be closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because this represents the land's value under the current rate method without restating the value.
FCX 61,390,000 × 0.0086 EUR/FCX = EUR 527,954 ≈ EUR 528,000
IFRS requires the foreign currency financial statements first to be restated for inflation using the procedures of IAS 29, and then the inflation-adjusted financial statements are translated using the current exchange rate. Non-monetary assets and non-monetary liabilities are restated for changes in the general purchasing power of the monetary unit. Most non-monetary items are carried at historical cost. In these cases, the restated cost is determined by applying to the historical cost the change in the general price index from the date of acquisition to the balance sheet date.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because this is the value of the land under US GAAP. Under US GAAP, the land is valued using the temporal method (historical cost at historical rate).
FCX 61,390,000 × 0.0149 EUR/FCX = EUR 914,711 ≈ EUR 915,000
US GAAP simply requires the foreign currency financial statements of such an entity to be translated as if the parent’s currency is the functional currency (i.e., the temporal method must be used with the resulting translation gain or loss reported in net income).
C. Correct.

vignettes.body:
Edel Asset Management is a long-short manager and manages portfolios primarily for endowment clients utilizing equities and listed options. Chief Investment Officer, Thomas Edel, is discussing the market environment with one of his portfolio managers, Anton Uder.
Edel explains to Uder: “I think it is important for us to be aware of the potential effects of unusual option trading volumes on markets as different types of risk become evident. Recently, discussion on a popular social media site promoted heavy purchases of short-term far out-of-the money call options on the stock of New Optics Technology (New Optics), a chain of eyeglass stores. New Optics is currently in financial difficulty, which has made it a favorite of short-sellers and it has a short interest of 85 million shares, which is over twenty times as large as its average daily volume. Call options volume was greatest in the calls with two weeks remaining to expiration with 1.46 million call options at a strike price of 90 being purchased by speculators. Each call option is a right to buy 100 shares of stock. Unlike in equities markets where there is a seller for every buyer, option contracts can be created by options dealers selling directly to speculators. They are able to do so by simultaneously delta hedging their own positions. The prices of the stock and option prices for New Optics Technology during the two weeks are shown in Exhibit 1.”
Exhibit 1
# Information | USD Price
Stock price 2 weeks before expiry | 47
90 Call price 2 weeks before expiry | 0.15
90 Put price 2 weeks before expiry | 42.97
Deltac  2 weeks before expiry | 0.057
Deltap  2 weeks before expiry | 0.989
Stock price 1 week before expiry | 90
Stock price at expiry | 140
Uder comments: I have determined that the volatility of the New Optics stock price in the 3 months prior to the options expiry was 23%, which would have been important information for options dealers two weeks before expiry, as it provided information regarding the perceived uncertainty going forward. The BSM options pricing model could have also been used to obtain information regarding future volatility."
Edel explains: "Option prices are also sensitive to a variety of factors derived from option valuation models. These factors are also referred to as the "Greeks", otherwise known as delta, gamma, theta, vega and rho, which are risk measures representing an option price's sensitivity to a particular factor. The same measure can simultaneously represent different types of risks to different market participants, such as options dealers and speculators."

questions.q: In response to the purchase of 1.46 million call options by speculators two weeks prior to expiry, the number of shares (in millions) that options dealers would likely have purchased in aggregate, is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect. The number of shares has been erroneously multiplied by Deltap 0.989 x 146 = 144.394.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect. Stock always has a Delta of 1 and it is not necessary to buy the same number of shares as the short options position if the Deltac is less than 1.

questions.q: Uder's comments on the importance of volatility information of the New Optics stock are most likely:
options: incorrect with respect to the use of the BSM model.
incorrect with respect to gauging uncertainty going forward.
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect. Uder is incorrect with respect to determining perceived uncertainty going forward, future uncertainty using historical volatility. Also, the correct measure is known as implied volatility. He is correct with regard to the use of the BSM model to calculate perceived uncertainty going forward, that is implied volatility.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect. The BSM model is indeed used to calculate volatility going forward, otherwise known as implied volatility.
C. Correct.

questions.q: The Greek letters representing the greatest risks to the two groups of market participants cited by Edel are most likely:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect. Delta is the change in the option for a change in the stock price. While related to gamma, it is not the primary risk for options dealers. Rho is the change in the option's price for a given change in the risk-free interest rate and is not a significant risk for speculators.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect. Vega is the change in the option price for a change in volatility. Dealers, hedge and seek to hold market neutral positions, would not be impacted by vega alone. Delta is the change in price of the option for a change in the stock price.
C. Correct.

questions.q: According to the data in Exhibit 1, the position resulting in the greatest USD profit beginning two weeks to expiry would most likely have been realized initiating a position combining:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect. The 90 puts would have cost 42.97 and would have expired worthless if the stock rose to 140. The 90 calls would have cost 0.15 and had a price of 50 at expiration resulting in a profit of 49.85 for the call and a loss of 42.97 for the put.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect. The 90 calls would hedge the short stock position after the stock price rose above 90, however the stocks would have had a loss between 47 and 90 of 43.  The terminal call price of 50 would have had the combination result in a net gain of 6.85 ((50-0.15)-43) = 6.85

vignettes.body:
Imane Kabbaj is the CIO of the Dynamo Fund, which is actively managed and invests in equities and bonds.
Kabbaj reviews the performance of the Dynamo Fund for the past year and focuses on the decomposition of the value added from asset allocation and security selection. Exhibit 1 reflects the return generated by the fund in each asset class compared to the relevant benchmark.
Exhibit 1
# Asset Class | Fund Return | Fund Allocation | Benchmark Return | Strategic Asset Allocation
Equities | –16% | 50% | –20% | 60%
Bonds | –12% | 50% | –10% | 40%
Kabbaj's goal for the fund's equity exposure is to maximize the Sharpe ratio by optimizing the allocation to active equity risk. She intends to invest in a combination of an active stock selection strategy and its benchmark, a global equity index. Based on the information in Exhibit 2, Kabbaj calculates the weight that should be allocated to the global equity index benchmark portfolio to achieve her goal.
Exhibit 2
#  | Active Stock Selection Strategy | Global Equity Index
Standard deviation of returns | 23% | 15%
Sharpe ratio | 0.47 | 0.53
Active risk | 9% | ---
Information ratio | 0.27 | ---
Next, Kabbaj analyzes the information in Exhibit 3, which shows the yields on corporate bonds, conventional government bonds, and inflation-linked government bonds issued in Country A with the same maturity, along with inflation expectations. She analyzes the bond risk premium to determine the market's confidence in inflation expectations being realized through the business cycle.
Exhibit 3
Corporate bond yield | 6.28%
Conventional government bond yield | 5.66%
Inflation-linked government bond yield | 2.32%
Survey-based inflation expectation | 2.80%
Kabbaj notes that P/E ratios for equities in Country A have recently increased to historically high levels. She observes that real interest rates, the equity risk premium, and real earnings growth expectations have also increased.

questions.q: For the Dynamo Fund, the value added from asset allocation over the past year was:
options: less than the value added from security selection.
equal to the value added from security selection.
greater than the value added from security selection.
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the value added from asset allocation is equal to the value added from security selection.
An example of how this conclusion may be derived is if value added from security selection is incorrectly calculated as follows:
The strategic asset allocation weights multiplied by the fund returns is [(60% × –16%) + (40% × –12%)] = –14.4%.
The benchmark return is [(60% × –20%) + (40% × –10%)] = –16.0%.
–14.4% – (–16.0%) = 1.6%, which may be interpreted as the value added from security selection, and this is greater than the value added from asset allocation (1.0%).
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the value added from asset allocation is equal to the value added from security selection.
An example of how this conclusion may be derived is as follows:
The strategic asset allocation weights multiplied by the fund returns is [(60% × –16%) + (40% × –12%)] = –14.4%.
The total fund return is [(50% × –16%) + (50% × –12%)] = –14.0%.
–14.0% – (–14.4%) = 0.4%, which may be interpreted as the value added from security selection, and this is less than the value added from asset allocation (1.0%).

questions.q: To achieve her goal for the equity exposure, the weight that Kabbaj should allocate to the global equity index benchmark portfolio is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the optimal amount of active risk is incorrectly calculated using the active stock selection strategy's standard deviation (σP) rather than that of the benchmark, as follows:
σ(RA) = (IR/SRB) × σP
σ(RA) = (0.27/0.53) × 23% = 11.72%
The weight on the active stock selection strategy would then be 11.72%/9.00% = 1.30 = 130%, and the weight on the benchmark portfolio would be 1 – 1.30 = –0.30 = –30% (i.e., short).
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because allocating 100% to the benchmark portfolio would give a Sharpe ratio of 0.53. This is higher than that of the active stock selection strategy but lower than the maximum Sharpe ratio of 0.595, which can be achieved through the combination of an allocation to both the active stock selection strategy and the benchmark portfolio.
The maximum Sharpe ratio based on a combination of benchmark portfolio and active stock selection strategy is calculated as:
SRP2 = SRB2 + IR2 = 0.532 + 0.272 = 0.3538
SRP = SQRT(0.3538) = 0.595

questions.q: The bond risk premium for uncertainty about future inflation in Country A is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the corporate bond yield is used as the starting point, however, this is incorrect as this would also include a credit premium.
The incorrect calculation is: Corporate bond yield less inflation-linked government bond yield less survey-based inflation expectation.
6.28% – 2.32% – 2.80% = 1.16%
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because this is calculated as conventional government bond yield less survey-based inflation expectation.
5.66% – 2.80% = 2.86%

questions.q: The change in which of the following factors best explains the recent level of P/E ratios in Country A?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because a high P/E could be the result of a number of factors, including the following: falling real interest rates. Therefore, increasing real interest rates will not result in higher P/E ratios.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because a high P/E could be the result of a number of factors, including the following: a decline in the equity risk premium. Therefore, an increase in the equity risk premium will not result in higher P/E ratios.
C. Correct.

vignettes.body:
Ulysses Emery is an analyst working on a research report on Zeta Incorporated, a manufacturing firm. The country in which Zeta operates has a flat income tax rate for corporations and a progressive income tax rate for individuals.
Emery reviews recent EPS and dividend per share (DPS) information for Zeta, presented in Exhibit 1. Zeta follows a target payout adjustment model for dividend payouts with a target payout ratio of 60%. Emery calculates the current year's expected DPS, assuming Zeta moves toward the target payout ratio over four years. Emery forecasts EPS of $2.44 for the current year.
Exhibit 1
#  | Most Recent Year | Two Years Ago | Three Years Ago | Four Years Ago
EPS | $2.13 | $1.33 | $2.41 | $2.24
DPS | $1.21 | $1.17 | $1.17 | $1.00
Payout ratio | 56.8% | 88.0% | 48.5% | 44.6%
The following week, Zeta announces its quarterly EPS, which matches market expectations, while its announced dividend is lower than what Emery and the market expected. Zeta's management justifies the announced dividend by stating that the firm faces near-term economic uncertainty in its major markets and needs to maintain its financial flexibility. Emery notes that Zeta's stock price rises after the dividend announcement.
Emery considers a scenario in which Zeta pays a 10% stock dividend and evaluates its impact on Zeta's financial statements.
Emery also covers Etaphi Company. He calculates Etaphi's FCFE coverage ratio using the financial information (in $ millions) in Exhibit 2.
Exhibit 2
Net interest paid | 6
Dividends paid | 76
Share issuance proceeds | 12
FCFE | 89

questions.q: Emery's forecast for Zeta's dividend per share for the current year should be closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because, on the basis that Zeta is assumed to move toward its target payout ratio over four years, the average payout ratio over the past four years is calculated and multiplied by the forecasted EPS. The sum of the past four dividends is $4.55 and the sum of the past four EPS is $8.11. Therefore, the average payout ratio is $4.55/$8.11 = 0.561; multiplying this by the forecasted EPS is 0.561 × $2.44 = $1.369 ≈ $1.37.
This distracter is also the closest response if the most recent year's payout ratio is used to estimate the dividend: 0.568 × $2.44 = $1.386 ≈ $1.39.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because this is the average dividend payout ratio over the most recent four years multiplied by $2.44, the EPS forecast:
(0.446 + 0.485 + 0.880 + 0.568) / 4 = 0.595; multiplying this by the earnings forecast of $2.44 equals $1.45.
This is also the closest answer if the target payout ratio (0.60) is multiplied by the $2.44 earnings forecast: 0.60 × $2.44 = $1.464 ≈ $1.46.

questions.q: Zeta's stock price movement following the dividend announcement is most consistent with:
options: the bird in the hand argument.
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because this theory states that investors can "make their own dividend" by selling (or purchasing) shares as appropriate, so the firm's dividend policy is irrelevant and does not affect firm value. But the theory behind this view assumes perfect capital markets and no taxes or transactions costs. Zeta is subject to a flat corporate tax rate and investors have a progressive tax rate schedule. Therefore, the assumption is violated. In addition, with a dividend below expectations, investors may have been expected to sell shares, thus reducing stock price, if 'homemade dividends' were an issue.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because this perspective will lead to a decline, not an increase, in stock price. Under the bird in the hand argument, investors prefer dividends now (cash in hand) rather than the risky and uncertain future capital gains. In addition, the announcement that dividends are lower than expected may create the possibility (due to product market uncertainty) for lower-than-expected earnings and dividends in the short-term future.
C. Correct.

questions.q: Which of the following would most likely change in the dividend scenario considered by Emery?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because cash is not affected by a stock dividend; stock dividends do not affect assets or liquidity ratios.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because stockholders' equity is not affected by stock dividends (offsetting changes in retained earnings and contributed capital keep stockholders' equity unchanged).

questions.q: Etaphi's FCFE coverage ratio is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the FCFE coverage ratio is computed as FCFE / [dividends + share repurchases]. Here, an incorrect calculation includes the new share issuance proceeds and net interest paid: $89 / [$76 – $12 + $6] = 1.2714 ≈ 1.27.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the FCFE coverage ratio is computed as FCFE / [dividends + share repurchases]. Here, an incorrect calculation includes the new share issuance proceeds: $89 / [$76 – $12] = 1.3906 ≈ 1.39.

vignettes.body:
Amine Ling manages a multi-asset portfolio that invests in the stocks and bonds of Country A and Country B.
Country A
Country A is a developing economy and its population growth rate will continue to be higher than that in developed economies. Country A's long-term goal is to accelerate economic growth so that its level of per capita income will eventually match that of developed economies. Country A intends to implement trade policies and develop legal, political, and economic institutions of developed countries to support this goal.
Country B
Ling researches Country B's labor market. She expects that in the next decade, Country B will experience the following changes:
Change 1: The unemployment rate will decline.
Change 2: The female labor force participation rate will rise.
Change 3: A greater proportion of the workforce will receive on-the-job training.
Ling estimates the potential GDP growth rate of Country B based on the labor productivity growth accounting equation and using her forecast of long-term growth rates in Exhibit 1.
Exhibit 1
Growth rate of labor force | –1.7%
Growth in total hours worked | –1.6%
Growth rate of labor productivity | 2.4%
Growth rate of total factor productivity | 0.8%
Ling intends to trade government bonds issued by Country A and Country B. Ling's outlook is that Country A's actual GDP growth rate will stay above the potential GDP growth rate and that Country B will experience much lower inflation than the current market forecast.

questions.q: The type of convergence occurring if Country A achieves its long-term goal is best referred to as:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because absolute convergence means that developing countries, regardless of their particular characteristics, will eventually catch up with the developed countries and match them in per capita output, whereas Ling believes Country A will converge if it introduces trade policies and successfully develops its legal, political, and economic institutions to support this goal. Furthermore, absolute convergence implies convergence of per capita growth rates among all countries. It does not, however, imply that the level of per capita income will be the same in all countries, whereas Country A plans to achieve the same income level of developed countries.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because conditional convergence means that convergence is conditional on the countries having the same saving rate, population growth rate, and production function. Country A has higher population growth than developed economies.

questions.q: Which expected change in Country B's labor market will most likely contribute to a permanent increase in its potential GDP growth?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because a reduction in the number of unemployed workers would boost utilization of the existing labor supply. This shift would represent a transition to a higher level of employment rather than a permanent increase in the potential growth rate of the economy, not the growth rate of employment. Unemployment is a transitory and not a permanent factor of the country's economic growth rate. Therefore, declining unemployment is not going to permanently change Country B’s economic growth rate.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because rising participation rates among women could increase growth in the labor force and in potential GDP. It should be noted, however, that rising or falling labor force participation is likely to represent a transition to a new higher or lower level of participation rather than a truly permanent rate of change. The rise in the female labor force participation rate is a transitory and not a permanent factor to the country's economic growth rate.
C. Correct.

questions.q: Based on the labor productivity growth accounting equation, the potential GDP growth rate of Country B is:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because it erroneously includes the growth in total hours worked. Growth rate of potential GDP = Growth in total hours worked + Long-term growth rate of labor force + Long-term growth rate in labor productivity = –1.6% – 1.7% + 2.4% = –0.9%.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because it erroneously includes the growth in total factor productivity. Growth rate of potential GDP = Growth in total factor productivity + Long-term growth rate of labor force + Long-term growth rate in labor productivity = 0.8% – 1.7% + 2.4% = 1.5%.

questions.q: Based on Ling's outlook, which country's bonds would most likely increase in price?
options: Both Country A's bonds and Country B's bonds
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because actual GDP growth above (below) the potential GDP growth rate puts upward (downward) pressure on inflation, which puts corresponding pressure on nominal interest rates and bond prices. Ling expects Country A's actual GDP growth rate will stay above the potential GDP growth rate. This leads to higher inflation and lower, not higher, bond prices.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because actual GDP growth above (below) the potential GDP growth rate puts upward (downward) pressure on inflation, which puts corresponding pressure on nominal interest rates and bond prices. Ling expects Country B will experience much lower inflation than the current market forecast. This leads to higher bond prices for Country B. Ling expects Country A's actual GDP growth rate will stay above the potential GDP growth rate. This leads to higher inflation and lower, not higher, bond prices.

vignettes.body:
Joel Dlamini, a private equity fund manager, is evaluating several potential investment opportunities for his portfolio.
Romala Enterprises
Dlamini believes that the valuation of small, privately owned Romala Enterprises requires several adjustments to estimate the firm's earnings potential. He uses the following information to estimate Romala's normalized EBIT:
Romala's reported EBIT is $5 million.
Romala's CEO is not paid a salary; however, she receives an annual $800,000 dividend as compensation. The annual salary of a replacement CEO is estimated to be $600,000.
Romala's optimal level of debt is $5.5 million more than its current amount of outstanding debt. The firm's pretax cost of debt is 10%.
Romala's effective tax rate is 18%.
Dlamini then uses the information in Exhibit 1 and the expanded CAPM to calculate Romala's required return on equity. For this calculation, he concludes that an industry risk premium is not relevant for Romala.
Exhibit 1
Estimated beta | 1.5
Risk-free rate | 3.5%
Equity risk premium | 5.0%
Small stock risk premium | 2.0%
Company-specific risk premium | 1.0%
Dlamini plans to acquire a non-controlling minority interest in Romala. He determines Romala has an unadjusted equity value of $900 million. He estimates the discount for lack of marketability to be 15% and the control premium to be 10%. Dlamini calculates the current equity value of Romala by making adjustments for lack of control and lack of marketability.
Rhode Industries
Dlamini values Rhode Industries, a privately held company. He calculates Rhode's EV using the FCFF valuation approach and the information in Exhibit 2.
Exhibit 2
Base-year FCFF (Year 0) | $1.2 million
Terminal value at the end of Year 2 | $15.4 million
WACC | 12.0%
Required return on equity | 14.5%
Initial growth rate | 6.0%
Initial high-growth period | 2 years

questions.q: Romala's normalized EBIT (in $ millions) is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the normalized earnings after interest and tax (EAIT) is calculated (instead of EBIT) as follows:
Normalized EAIT = Reported EBIT – CEO salary – Increase in interest paid + Tax benefit on interest paid
Interest paid = $5,500,000 × 0.10 = $550,000
Tax benefit on interest paid = $550,000 × 0.18 = $99,000
Normalized EAIT = $5,000,000 – $600,000 – $550,000 + $99,000
= $3,949,000 ≈ $3.9 million
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the normalized EBIT for Romala is calculated by deducting the net difference between the current CEO's compensation and a replacement CEO's salary ($800,000 – $600,000 = $200,000):
Normalized EBIT = Reported EBIT – Net difference in CEO salary
= $5,000,000 – $200,000
= $4,800,000 = $4.8 million
No adjustment to EBIT was correctly taken into account for the increase in debt level as interest and its effect on taxes are below the EBIT line.

questions.q: The required return on equity for Romala using the expanded CAPM is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the calculation for the required return on equity for Romala does not adjust the equity risk premium for beta.
= 3.5% + 5.0% + 2.0% + 1.0%
= 11.5%
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the required return on equity for Romala using the CAPM omits the small stock risk premium:
re = rf + β(rm – rf) + Company-specific risk premium
= 3.5% + (1.5 × 5.0%) + 1.0%
= 12.0%
C. Correct.

questions.q: Romala's adjusted equity value (in $ millions) is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the total discount is calculated incorrectly by adding the DLOC and DLOM as follows:
Adjusted equity value = Unadjusted equity value – Total discount
Total discount = 1 – (DLOC + DLOM)
where:
DLOC = Discount for lack of control
DLOM = Discount for lack of marketability
DLOM is given in the case as 15%, but DLOC has to be calculated first:
DLOC = 1 – [1/(1 + Control premium)]
= 1 – [1/(1 + 0.10)]
≈ 1 – 0.9091
≈ 0.0909 = 9.09%
Total discount is calculated as:
≈ 0.0909 + 0.1500
≈ 0.2409 ≈ 24.09%
And then the adjusted equity value is $900 million × (1 – 0.2409) ≈ $683.18 million ≈ $683 million.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the DLOC is not calculated correctly and merely multiplied with the DLOM as follows:
Total discount is calculated as:
= 1 – [(1 – 0.10) × (1 – 0.15)]
= 1 – 0.7650
= 0.2350 = 23.5%
And then the adjusted equity value is $900 million × (1 – 0.2350) = $688.5 million ≈ $689 million.
C. Correct.

questions.q: Using the FCFF valuation approach, Rhode's enterprise value (in $ millions) is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because Rhode's enterprise value is calculated using the FCFF valuation approach but discounts the terminal value for three years as follows:
EV = FCFF1/(1 + WACC) + FCFF2/(1 + WACC)2 + TV/(1 + WACC)3
where:
EV = Enterprise value
TV = Terminal value (given in the case as $15.4 million)
EV = ($1,200,000 × 1.06)/(1.12) + ($1,200,000 × (1.06)2)/(1.12)2 + $15,400,000/(1.12)3
≈ ($1,272,000/1.12) + ($1,348,320/1.2544) + $15,400,000/(1.4049)
≈ $1,135,714 + $1,074,872 + $10,961,416
≈ $13,172,003
≈ $13.2 million
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because Rhode's enterprise value is calculated using the FCFF valuation approach with required return on equity as the discount rate as follows:
EV = FCFF1/(1 + r) + FCFF2/(1 + r)2 + TV/(1 + r)2
where:
EV = Enterprise value
TV = Terminal value (given in the case as $15.4 million)
EV = ($1,200,000 × 1.06)/(1.145) + ($1,200,000 × (1.06)2)/(1.145)2 + $15,400,000/(1.145)2
≈ ($1,272,000/1.145) + ($1,348,320/1.3110) + ($15,400,000/1.3110)
≈ $1,110,917 + $1,028,447 + $11,746,534
≈ $13,885,898
≈ $13.9 million
C. Correct.
